sm: The Williamson County Public Health Committee met on November fifth. It elected Ricky Jones as chair and Nancy Bailey as vice chair, both by voice vote, and approved the April second minutes. The committee then took up an annual resolution authorizing the mayor to sign agreements for opioid remediation and abatement services, funded from opioid settlement money. A speaker explained that the opioid task force, working with an office of public health at a university for expert review, received about one point seven million dollars in requests against roughly one million available, so some projects were funded in part and others not. Unfunded applicants will be contacted after the commission meeting and can ask for feedback. The resolution passed unanimously. The committee then began an interlocal agreement for emergency ambulance services with the hospital district, Williamson Health, the City of Springfield and Murray County, Tennessee, noting that one point five million dollars had been withheld from the hospital last budget cycle while service continued to the Murray County side of Spring Hill.

The presenter explained that if Murray County approves, it would pay seven hundred fifty thousand dollars for January through July, then one point five million dollars for the next budget cycle, with a built-in escalator after that. A committee member questioned section 10.3, which says the fee rises automatically by three percent each year but also says it stays the same if the county fails to give notice by May first. Staff said the clause means the fee can rise by no more than three percent without renegotiation, and that the county must notify Murray County of the amount. Staff said contract tracking and reminders in the county law office and the mayor's office would make sure notices go out. Staff added that the agreement runs eighteen months, and later extensions would not return to the committee unless material terms change. Another member asked about section 10.5, where late payments accrue interest at one percent, and it was unclear whether that means one percent per month, or twelve percent a year, or one percent annually.

The discussion continued on the interest rate, and staff agreed to check whether it is monthly or annual. One member said they would not support a one percent annual rate. Another member asked what happens if the pending hospital sale to Ascension closes, possibly by 2028, and whether the successor would be bound. Staff pointed to termination language, including section 11.2, and a clause in 11.3 saying the agreement is not assignable. They promised to research the interest rate and termination questions before the Monday meeting. Staff said the agreement would take effect January first, with seven hundred fifty thousand dollars covering January through June of 2027, and one point five million dollars covering July 2027 through June 2028. Notice duties technically fall to the mayor, often carried out by the county attorney's office or mayor's staff. The resolution passed unanimously, there was no other business, and the meeting adjourned.
